# Sending Logs to Amazon S3

## Overview

When logs are published directly to Amazon S3, they go to an existing bucket that you specify. One or more log files are created every five minutes in that bucket. When logs are delivered to an S3 bucket for the first time, the log-delivering service records the bucket owner. This ensures logs are delivered only to a bucket belonging to this account. If you later change the S3 bucket owner, you must re-create or update the log subscription in the originating service.

CloudFront uses a different permissions model than other services that send vended logs to S3. If the same S3 bucket is used for CloudFront access logs and another log source, enabling ACL on the bucket for CloudFront grants permission to all other log sources using the bucket.

## Required permissions

The permissions you need depend on whether this is your first log type to the bucket. To set up sending logs to S3 for the first time, you need the `logs:CreateLogDelivery`, `S3:GetBucketPolicy`, and `S3:PutBucketPolicy` permissions. If another of these log types is already being sent to the same S3 bucket, setting up another log type to that bucket needs only the `logs:CreateLogDelivery` permission.

## Bucket resource policy

The S3 bucket receiving logs must have a resource policy that includes certain permissions, which let the log delivery account write to the bucket. AWS creates or changes the resource policies of the bucket as needed. The outcome depends on the bucket's current state:

- If the bucket currently has no resource policy, and the user setting up logging has `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy` permissions for the bucket, AWS automatically creates the log delivery policy for the bucket when logs begin being sent.
- If the bucket has a resource policy that lacks the log delivery statement, and the user has those same permissions, the log delivery statement is appended to the bucket's resource policy.

### Buckets with NotAction or NotPrincipal

If the S3 bucket policy contains a `NotAction` or `NotPrincipal` element, automatically adding the log delivery permissions to the bucket and creating a log subscription fails. In that case, manually add the log delivery permissions to the bucket policy and then create the log subscription. Creating the log subscription then succeeds.

### CloudTrail AccessDenied errors

AccessDenied errors may appear in CloudTrail if `s3:ListBucket` has not been granted to `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`. To avoid these errors, grant `s3:ListBucket` to `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`, using the same Condition parameters shown for `s3:GetBucketAcl`. You can do this by updating the `AWSLogDeliveryAclCheck` statement to have Action `[s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:ListBucket]`.

## Server-side encryption

**SSE-S3:** This requires no additional configuration, because Amazon S3 handles the encryption key.

**SSE-KMS:** If you choose SSE-KMS for the bucket, you must use a customer managed key. Using an AWS managed key is not supported for this scenario. If encryption is set up using an AWS managed key, logs are delivered in an unreadable format.

When the S3 bucket has server-side encryption using a customer managed AWS KMS key, the key policy for that key must also include the log delivery permissions. The key policy statement for `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com` must be added to the customer managed key's key policy, not the bucket policy.

Two further considerations apply to KMS-encrypted buckets:

- If the destination bucket has SSE-KMS with a Bucket Key enabled, the attached customer managed KMS key policy no longer works as expected for all requests.
- If you use vended logs with S3 encryption using a customer managed KMS key, you must use a fully qualified AWS KMS key ARN instead of a key ID when configuring the bucket.

Logs published directly to Amazon S3 go to an existing bucket that you specify. One or more log files are created in that bucket every five minutes. The first time logs are delivered to an S3 bucket, the log-delivering service records the bucket owner. This ensures logs are delivered only to a bucket belonging to this account. If you change the bucket owner, you must re-create or update the log subscription in the originating service. If needed, AWS creates or changes the resource policies of the receiving bucket.

The permissions you need depend on whether the bucket is already receiving logs. To set up sending logs to S3 for the first time, you need the `logs:CreateLogDelivery`, `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy` permissions. If another of these log types is already being sent to the same bucket, you need only `logs:CreateLogDelivery` to set up another log type. The receiving bucket must have a resource policy that includes certain permissions, which allow the log delivery account to write to it. If the bucket currently has no resource policy and you have `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy` for the bucket, AWS automatically creates the log delivery policy when logs begin being sent. If the bucket already has a resource policy that lacks the log delivery statement, that statement is appended to it.

AccessDenied errors may appear in CloudTrail if `s3:ListBucket` has not been granted to `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`. To avoid them, grant `s3:ListBucket` to `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`, using the same Condition parameters shown for `s3:GetBucketAcl`. You can do this by updating the `AWSLogDeliveryAclCheck` statement to have the Action `[s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:ListBucket]`.

Encryption options also affect configuration. SSE-S3 requires no additional configuration, because Amazon S3 handles the encryption key. If you choose SSE-KMS for the bucket, you must use a customer managed key, since an AWS managed key is not supported for this scenario. If encryption is set up with an AWS managed key, logs are delivered in an unreadable format. When the bucket uses server-side encryption with a customer managed AWS KMS key, the key policy must also include the log delivery permissions. The key policy statement for `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com` must be added to the customer managed key's key policy, not the bucket policy. If the destination bucket has SSE-KMS with a Bucket Key enabled, the attached customer managed KMS key policy no longer works as expected for all requests. When you use vended logs with S3 encryption using a customer managed KMS key, you must use a fully qualified AWS KMS key ARN rather than a key ID when configuring the bucket.

Two further cases need special handling. CloudFront uses a different permissions model than other services that send vended logs to S3. If the same S3 bucket is used for CloudFront access logs and another log source, enabling ACL on the bucket for CloudFront grants permission to all other log sources using the bucket. If the S3 bucket policy contains a `NotAction` or `NotPrincipal` element, automatically adding log delivery permissions to the bucket and creating a log subscription fails. In that case, manually add the log delivery permissions to the bucket policy and then create the log subscription, which then succeeds.

# Sending vended logs to Amazon S3

## Before you begin

Make sure you have the following in place before you start.

- **An existing S3 bucket to receive the logs.** Logs published directly to Amazon S3 go to an existing bucket that you specify as the destination for log delivery.
- **User permissions for first-time setup.** The account setting up logging for the first time needs `logs:CreateLogDelivery`, `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy`.
- **An S3 bucket resource policy that grants log delivery permissions to `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`.** AWS creates this automatically if you have the permissions above. You must add it manually if the bucket policy contains a `NotAction` or `NotPrincipal` element. The steps are in the sections below.
- **A customer managed AWS KMS key, if you use SSE-KMS.** An AWS managed key is not supported. Reference the key by its fully qualified ARN.
- **A KMS key policy statement that lets the log delivery service use the customer managed key, if the bucket uses SSE-KMS.** The steps are in the encryption section below.

## How delivery works

Logs published directly to Amazon S3 are published to an existing bucket that you specify. One or more log files are created every five minutes in that bucket.

The first time logs are delivered to an S3 bucket, the log-delivering service records the bucket owner. This ensures logs are delivered only to a bucket belonging to this account. Because the owner is recorded, changing the S3 bucket owner later requires you to re-create or update the log subscription in the originating service.

If you set up another log type to a bucket that already receives one of these log types, you need only the `logs:CreateLogDelivery` permission. The `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy` permissions are needed only for the first-time setup.

CloudFront uses a different permissions model from other services that send vended logs to S3. If the same S3 bucket is used for CloudFront access logs and another log source, enabling ACL on the bucket for CloudFront grants permission to all other log sources using that bucket.

## Bucket resource policy

The S3 bucket receiving logs must have a resource policy that includes certain permissions. AWS creates or changes this policy if needed.

- **The bucket has no resource policy.** If the user setting up logging has `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy` permissions for the bucket, AWS automatically creates the log delivery policy when logs begin being sent. This happens only when both conditions hold: the bucket has no policy and you have both permissions.
- **The bucket has a resource policy that lacks the log delivery statement.** If you also have `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy` permissions for the bucket, the log delivery statement is appended to the existing policy. This happens only when both conditions hold.
- **The bucket policy contains a `NotAction` or `NotPrincipal` element.** Automatically adding log delivery permissions to the bucket and creating a log subscription then fails. In this case, first add the log delivery permissions to the bucket policy manually, and then create the log subscription. The subscription creation succeeds only when you hold `logs:CreateLogDelivery`, `S3:GetBucketPolicy` and `S3:PutBucketPolicy`.

### Avoiding CloudTrail AccessDenied errors

AccessDenied errors may appear in CloudTrail if `s3:ListBucket` has not been granted to `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`. Granting `s3:ListBucket` to `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com`, with the same `Condition` parameters shown for `s3:GetBucketAcl`, is enough to avoid these errors. To do this, update the `AWSLogDeliveryAclCheck` statement to have `Action` set to `[s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:ListBucket]`.

## Encryption

You can choose between two server-side encryption options for the bucket.

**SSE-S3.** This requires no additional configuration, because Amazon S3 handles the encryption key.

**SSE-KMS.** If you choose SSE-KMS for the bucket, you must use a customer managed key. This means an AWS managed key is not supported for this scenario. If you set up encryption with an AWS managed key, logs are delivered in an unreadable format.

Because you chose SSE-KMS, add the key policy statement for `delivery.logs.amazonaws.com` to the customer managed key's key policy, not to the bucket policy. The log delivery account can write to the S3 bucket only when this key policy statement is in place. The key policy for the customer managed key must include the log delivery permissions whenever the bucket has server-side encryption using a customer managed AWS KMS key.

When you use vended logs with S3 encryption using a customer managed KMS key, you must use a fully qualified AWS KMS key ARN, not a key ID, when configuring the bucket.

If the destination bucket uses SSE-KMS with a Bucket Key enabled, the attached customer managed KMS key policy no longer works as expected for all requests.
